title: GRAND : Graph Reconstruction from potential partial Adjacency and Neighborhood Data

problem.claim: Private protocols that compute graph functions can leak sensitive information about the original graph structure.

gap.claim: The abstract addresses reconstruction from the matrix of common-neighbor counts, including cases with partial knowledge of the original graph.

contributions.claim: An approach reconstructs a graph's adjacency matrix from the result of a private protocol computing the number of common neighbors between all vertex pairs.
The work introduces co-squareness to characterize the ambiguity in reconstruction when different graphs have the same common-neighbors matrix.
The analysis considers an adversary observing only the common-neighbors matrix and a more informed adversary with partial knowledge of the original graph.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that graphs can be reconstructed with high accuracy from their common-neighbors matrix, up to co-squareness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Distributed graph functions can be computed securely without centralizing participants' data.
Protocol outputs may reveal sensitive information about the graph structure.
The proposed approach reconstructs the adjacency matrix from common-neighbor counts observed from a private protocol.
Reconstruction is limited by co-squareness, and the work studies two levels of adversary knowledge.
The authors report high-accuracy reconstruction up to co-squareness and note graph-theoretic interest.

source_observation.claim: Outputs of privacy-preserving graph protocols may enable reconstruction of sensitive structure.

interpretation.claim: Protecting the input data does not by itself ensure that derived graph statistics are non-informative.

application.claim: Assess whether released graph statistics permit adjacency or structural reconstruction before treating a protocol output as private.

exception.claim: Reconstruction may be ambiguous when different graphs share the same common-neighbors matrix.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the reconstruction algorithm.
The abstract does not provide datasets, accuracy values, baselines, or evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not define co-squareness formally.
